SPEC_GAP. The landed topology erases the pcurve payload at the Wire boundary; no file in write_allow can change that, and no in-scope parallel representation exists. Empirical proof follows. (1) ANCHORS — all six verified by grep, each count == 1: A1 `pub struct Edge` (truck-topology/src/lib.rs:125); A3 `pcurve: Option` field (lib.rs:128); A2 `pub struct Wire` (lib.rs:137); A4 `edge_list: VecDeque>` (lib.rs:138); A5 `pub fn with_pcurve(self, pcurve: Q) -> Edge` (truck-topology/src/edge.rs:529); A6 `pub struct PCurve` (truck-geometry/src/decorators/mod.rs:222). (2) STRUCT DEFINITIONS READ — `Edge { vertices: (Vertex

, Vertex

), orientation: bool, pcurve: Option, curve: Arc }` (lib.rs:125-130); `Wire { edge_list: VecDeque> }` (lib.rs:137-139); `Face { boundaries: Vec>, orientation: bool, surface: Arc }` (lib.rs:157-161); `Shell { face_list: Vec> }` (lib.rs:168-170); `Solid { boundaries: Vec> }` (lib.rs:174-176). PC appears NOWHERE above Wire: `Wire` writes `Edge` which, by the A1 default, is `Edge`. (3) TYPE-PARAMETER ERASURE — A5 changes the type parameter: `with_pcurve` returns `Edge`. A real pcurve therefore yields `Edge>`, which cannot occupy `VecDeque>`; a `Wire` can only hold pcurve-less edges. So a pcurve can never ride on a boundary edge of any Face/Shell/Solid: threading it would require adding PC to Wire -> Face -> Shell -> Solid, a cross-crate topology-wide type change touching every Wire use across meshalgo/shapeops/modeling/stepio — the future program BG-CE-001 anticipated ('the packet that wires real pcurves owns trace splitting'), not an S2 follow-up. The truck-topology test modules confirm the container-side blocker from the inside: they attach `i32`/`PCurve, Plane>` payloads only to STANDALONE edges (`Edge::new(...).with_pcurve(...)` in edge.rs:793-851 and invariants/same_parameter.rs:338-340, 365, 461, 485) — never to an edge inside a Wire. (4) COMPILE PROBE — scratch crate in the temp dir (outside the repo, not committed) against the landed aliases (`truck_topology::prelude!(Point3, Curve, Surface, pub)` in truck-modeling/src/lib.rs:35 => `Edge` = `Edge`, `Wire` = `Wire`). Built `edge.with_pcurve(PCurve::new(Line, Plane))` then `Wire::from(vec![pcurved_edge])`. Result: exactly one error, E0277 — 'the trait bound `VecDeque, Curve>>: From>>` is not satisfied'; 'the trait `From, Curve, PCurve>, Plane>>>>` is not implemented for `VecDeque, Curve>>`'; 'required for `Wire, Curve>` to implement `From, Curve, PCurve>, Plane>>>>`'. The pcurve-carrying edge cannot enter a Wire; the value side (`PCurve`, A6) is fine, the container side is the blocker. (5) IN-SCOPE REPRESENTATION — none exists. The booked API `extrude_profile(&[Curve], &Arrangement, f64) -> Outcome` (plan §4; docs/SOLVER_FAMILY_PLAN.md; extrude.rs:52-56) returns only the Solid; the `Certificate` it wraps carries only evidence props (Method::Exact, CoedgePairing/VertexLink/AnalyticCarrier), no per-face geometry channel. The topology's `tolerance_store`/`entity_id` sidecars (truck-topology/src/lib.rs:388, 399) are not pcurve carriers and are read-only here. A parallel per-face pcurve table would require a NEW public return channel (changed or added signature) that the landed API does not book — that is API design work, not an in-scope implementation — and it would not make pcurves 'ride on the edges of the returned Solid': a Phase-4 consumer walking the Solid would have to re-match boundary edges positionally against a detached table with no invariant tying table rows to topology edges. The packet's feasible-representation conditions (a)+(b)+(c) are therefore not genuinely met; extrude.rs:21 itself records 'PC = () (no pcurves — a documented later refinement)', and no write_allow file can erase the erasure. (6) CONSEQUENCE — SPEC_GAP, per the packet's section 1 decision: the plan §4 Phase 2 'pcurves' line and M1's 'exercises pcurves' cannot be delivered on the returned Solid's edges without the cross-crate PC-threading program.
